enhanced.fullText:
The Federal Insurance Contributions Act (FICA), codified at 26 U.S.C. §§ 3101-3128, establishes the framework for Social Security and Medicare taxation for employers and employees, including higher education institutions. Under 26 U.S.C. § 3121(b)(10), FICA provides a critical exemption for student employees that significantly impacts university payroll operations and tax compliance.

The student exemption under 26 U.S.C. § 3121(b)(10) exempts services performed by students who are enrolled and regularly attending classes at the employing educational institution from FICA taxation. This exemption applies to both the employer's 7.65% contribution and the employee's 7.65% withholding for Social Security (6.2%) and Medicare (1.45%) taxes. The Internal Revenue Service interprets 'regularly attending classes' through Revenue Ruling 2005-11, which requires students to carry a course load that is at least half of the full-time equivalent as determined by the institution.

Under 26 U.S.C. § 3111, universities must pay the employer portion of FICA taxes for all non-exempt employees. The exemption extends beyond traditional undergraduate students to include graduate students, postdoctoral fellows, and continuing education students who meet enrollment criteria. However, per 26 C.F.R. § 31.3121(b)(10)-2, the exemption terminates immediately when students cease enrollment or drop below half-time status.

Additionally, 26 U.S.C. § 3121(b)(8)(A) provides an exemption for clergy members performing services in the exercise of their ministry, including university chaplains and theology faculty with ministerial duties. This exemption requires careful documentation of the religious nature of services performed.

Universities must maintain detailed payroll records per 26 C.F.R. § 31.6001-1, documenting student enrollment status, course loads, and employment periods to substantiate exemption claims. The IRS may impose penalties under 26 U.S.C. § 6656 for failure to deposit required FICA taxes, with penalties ranging from 2% to 15% of unpaid taxes depending on the delay period. Additional penalties under 26 U.S.C. § 6721 apply for incorrect Form W-2 reporting, with fines up to $280 per form.

Recent guidance in Notice 2013-54 clarified that student loan forgiveness programs may trigger FICA liability for amounts forgiven as compensation. Universities must also comply with the Affordable Care Act's additional Medicare tax of 0.9% under 26 U.S.C. § 3101(b)(2) for employees earning over $200,000 annually, with no student exemption available for this additional tax.
enhanced.summary: FICA requires universities to pay Social Security and Medicare taxes on employee wages, with exemptions for enrolled students meeting half-time attendance requirements and qualifying clergy performing ministerial duties.
enhanced.requirements:
## Student Exemption Administration
- Verify student enrollment and half-time status before each pay period per 26 U.S.C. § 3121(b)(10)
- Document course loads through registrar records and academic transcripts
- Terminate exemptions immediately upon withdrawal or reduction below half-time status

## Payroll Tax Compliance
- Calculate and withhold employee FICA taxes at 7.65% for non-exempt employees under 26 U.S.C. § 3102
- Pay employer matching contributions of 7.65% for all taxable wages per 26 U.S.C. § 3111
- Apply additional 0.9% Medicare tax withholding for high earners exceeding $200,000 annually

## Record Maintenance Requirements
- Maintain enrollment verification documentation per 26 C.F.R. § 31.6001-1
- Preserve payroll records for four years following tax due dates
- Document ministerial exemptions with detailed job descriptions and religious duties
enhanced.reportingRequirements: Quarterly Form 941 filing by last day of month following quarter end. Semi-weekly tax deposits required for large employers within three business days. Annual Form W-2 distribution to employees by January 31st with Copy A filed with SSA by same deadline per 26 C.F.R. § 31.6051-1.
